parameters.content:
## Expansion Opportunity Detection Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: Weekly scoring run; instant Webhook triggers for high-value signals like hitting a plan limit or a pricing-page visit by an admin.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Scores explain themselves — each account shows the signals behind it.
   - Accounts with an open escalation, a churn-risk flag or a renewal within 30 days are excluded or routed to a different play.
   - The agent drafts openers; CSMs send them. No automated upsell emails.
   - Weights are tuned from tracked outcomes, quarterly, by RevOps.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/expansion-opportunity-detection/
Want it built and run for you? $297/month · custom $4,500–8,000 one-time

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger (weekly)
nodes.notes:
Schedule Trigger (weekly) + instant triggers

Weekly scoring run; instant Webhook triggers for high-value signals like hitting a plan limit or a pricing-page visit by an admin.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Product analytics (Amplitude, Mixpanel, Pendo, PostHog)
- Billing and entitlements (Stripe, Chargebee, in-house)
- CRM accounts, ARR, renewal dates, owners (HubSpot, Salesforce)
- Web analytics (pricing-page visits) and enrichment (Clearbit, Apollo)

parameters.notes: Active users, seats used vs. purchased, feature adoption, API/usage volume vs. plan limits from product analytics and billing; ARR, plan, renewal date and owner from the CRM.

Active users, seats used vs. purchased, feature adoption, API/usage volume vs. plan limits from product analytics and billing; ARR, plan, renewal date and owner from the CRM.

parameters.notes: Pricing-page visits, webinar attendance, support questions about premium features, new integrations connected, and firmographic changes (funding, hiring) from enrichment tools.

nodes.name: HTTP Request: Pull engagement and buying signals
nodes.notes:
Pull engagement and buying signals

Pricing-page visits, webinar attendance, support questions about premium features, new integrations connected, and firmographic changes (funding, hiring) from enrichment tools.

nodes.name: Code: Compute the readiness score
nodes.notes:
Compute the readiness score

Weighted score per account from usage growth, limit proximity, adoption breadth, engagement and buying signals; weights per segment live in a sheet the RevOps lead can tune.

nodes.name: Switch: Match to a play
nodes.notes:
Match to a play

Signal pattern → play: seat expansion, tier upgrade, add-on module, multi-year, or a 'not yet' hold. Each play has a target offer, a talk track and a timing rule.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Draft the opener" step of the Expansion Opportunity Detection Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: For each account on the list the agent writes a three-sentence opener for the CSM, grounded in the account's actual usage and phrased as help, not a pitch. CSMs edit before sending.

Rules:
- Scores explain themselves — each account shows the signals behind it.
- Accounts with an open escalation, a churn-risk flag or a renewal within 30 days are excluded or routed to a different play.
- The agent drafts openers; CSMs send them. No automated upsell emails.
- Weights are tuned from tracked outcomes, quarterly, by RevOps.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: AI Agent: Draft the opener
nodes.notes:
Draft the opener

For each account on the list the agent writes a three-sentence opener for the CSM, grounded in the account's actual usage and phrased as help, not a pitch. CSMs edit before sending.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Draft the opener
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: HubSpot: Route to the owner
nodes.notes:
Route to the owner

Creates or updates an expansion opportunity on the account with the score, signals and play; posts the CSM's weekly list to Slack.

nodes.name: Postgres: Track outcomes by signal
nodes.notes:
Track outcomes by signal

Every surfaced opportunity is tracked to won/lost/ignored, so the score weights are tuned quarterly from what actually converted.
